findings.title: ERB `end if` is a syntax error and breaks the best view
findings.body: The closing tag is `<%- end if %>` with no condition after `if`. ERB compiles this to invalid Ruby, so any request that renders the `best` template (i.e. whenever a TopicEmbed exists) raises a template error/500 instead of showing the embedded discussion. The closing tag should be `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: raw_html imports bypass sanitization and enable stored XSS
findings.body: `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, and `TopicEmbed.import` sets that for RSS/Readability content while `PollFeed` even calls `CGI.unescapeHTML` on it. `TopicEmbed.import` also interpolates the feed URL directly into an `<a href='...'>` footer. The imported HTML is stored unsanitized and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` renders it with `raw post.cooked`. A feed containing `<script>`, event handlers, or `javascript:` URLs therefore executes in the Discourse origin. Sanitize the HTML before storing/serving it, or keep imported posts on the normal cook path.

findings.title: PollFeed assumes every RSS item has `content`
findings.body: `i.content` is not defined for standard RSS items that only provide `<description>` or `<summary>`. Calling `.scrub` on nil raises NoMethodError, and because PollFeed has retry disabled a single such item aborts the hourly polling run so later items are never imported. Use a fallback such as `i.content || i.description` and guard against nil.

findings.title: Updating a TopicEmbed whose post was deleted raises and stops feed polling
findings.body: When an existing embed is found, `post = embed.post` is used without checking whether the post still exists. If the imported topic/post was deleted, `embed.post` can be nil; on a content change `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!` then dereferences nil and raises, aborting the whole PollFeed run (retry is disabled). Remove or repair stale TopicEmbed rows before revising.

findings.title: Open-uri fetch follows redirects and permits SSRF
findings.body: `open(url).read` performs an unrestricted outbound request. The only host validation, `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, checks the original URI host; `open-uri` follows redirects, so an allowed embeddable host that has an open redirect can make the Discourse server fetch localhost/internal services or cloud metadata and then import the response into a post. Validate redirect targets and block private addresses, and add timeouts/size limits.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring instead of exact origin
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that appears as a substring of the configured Discourse URL. For example, with discourseUrl `http://example.com/`, an origin `http://example.co` passes, so another frame can send `discourse-resize` messages and alter the iframe height. Parse discourseUrl and compare the scheme/host/port exactly.

findings.title: Success spec leaves @topic_view nil and cannot pass
findings.body: `TopicView.expects(:new).with(...)` has no `.returns(...)`, so the controller assigns nil to @topic_view. The rendered `best` view immediately calls `@topic_view.posts` and raises NoMethodError, so the after block expecting a successful response fails. Stub TopicView.new to return a view object with a topic and posts.

findings.title: PollFeed guard tests are vacuous
findings.body: The tests for missing feed_polling_url and missing embed_by_username do not stub feed_polling_enabled? to true, and the default is false. The execute condition therefore short-circuits before reaching the setting under test, so these specs pass even if the URL/username guards are removed. Stub the other required settings to true.
